method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024' (published online 30 January 2025), 25 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at licence line in the publisher PDF (open-access copy from IRIS UNIMORE; the HAL copy was behind a bot challenge and was not used)). S2: QUOTED from Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124) 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature' (published 11 September 2024), 12 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11430793). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. The guideline's own disclaimer also states (verbatim): 'This work is fully copyrighted. Unauthorized use outside the provisions of the copyright act, without written permission from the GPO of the EADO, is prohibited. This includes duplication, translation, microfilming, and the use and application of electronic systems, intranets, and the internet.' Recorded per the standing owner decision; the article's CC BY-NC-ND licence governs and the content is paraphrased. Edition 2.0 keeps every S1 claim unchanged and adds S2, a CC BY 2024 narrative review, quoted, for staging systems, margin-width data, imatinib and neoadjuvant outcomes, radiotherapy detail and prognosis. The file dermatofibrosarcoma-protuberans.layout.txt is a second extraction of S1 (same guideline), not a second source; no second open DFSP guideline was found in one Europe PMC search.

claims.claim: **DFSP is a rare fibroblastic skin tumour that invades locally and recurs, but seldom spreads.** Diagnosis is often late, so tumours are large; it grows as irregular, finger-like projections well beyond what is visible.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incidence is under 1 per 100,000 a year; most patients are 20 to 59.** Survival is excellent (5-year DFSP-specific survival 99.2%).
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It usually starts as a slow, painless, firm plaque of 2 to 5 cm,** most often on the trunk. A sudden growth spurt may mean fibrosarcomatous change.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Think of DFSP when a solitary 'keloid' or hypertrophic scar has no history of injury or surgery;** a small punch biopsy before any big excision avoids mistreatment.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fibrosarcomatous DFSP (10–15% of cases) is more aggressive,** with metastasis risk of 15–20%: stage with CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis plus nodal ultrasound.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm on histology before extensive surgery.** (A)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a deep incisional biopsy, ideally reported by a sarcoma or dermatopathology expert;** keep formalin fixation to 72 h or less so molecular tests remain possible. Diffuse strong CD34 staining is typical.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use CD34 in every suspected case, and re-biopsy if suspicion stays high after a non-diagnostic sample.**
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reports must state whether high mitotic rate or fibrosarcomatous change is present.** (A)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Molecular testing (FISH for COL1A1::PDGFB, present in more than 90%) should be done where possible** (B); about 8% are FISH-negative and may need RNA sequencing or expert review.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contrast MRI can map extent before surgery (C),** especially for tumours over 3 cm, head and neck sites, lesions near bone or joints, or recurrences. Staging scans are not routine except for suspected metastasis, recurrence or FS-DFSP (B).
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ultrasound (7.5–10 MHz) or MRI can assess extent before surgery;** with suspected recurrence or distant disease, add lymph node ultrasound and CT or MRI.
claims.source_text: Both ultrasound (7.5-10 MHz) and magnetic resonance imaging can be useful in assessing the extent of the tumor prior to surgery. With suspected local recurrent and/or distant disease, lymph node ultrasound and cross-sectional imaging by computed tomography or magnetic resonance are of value [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **There is no definitive DFSP staging system.** NCCN uses stage I local, II regional and III distant disease; the 2018 German guideline uses stage I primary tumour, II lymph node metastasis and III distant metastasis. Some apply the AJCC soft-tissue sarcoma system.
claims.source_text: To date, there is no definitive staging system for DFSP. Some authors apply the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) Staging Protocol for Sarcoma of Soft Tissue classification []. Others studies use a straightforward distinction: primary tumor vs. local recurrence []. The NCCN classification is as follows: stage I is local disease, stage II is regional disease, and stage III is distant disease []. Somewhat similarly, the 2018 German dermatologic-oncologic practice guidelines provide the following simplified classification: stage I-primary tumor (localized disease); stage II-lymph node metastasis; stage III-distant metastasis [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Deaths are rare but cluster in large or high-grade tumours:** in 7567 SEER patients, 89 (1.18%) died of DFSP, with higher disease-specific mortality at 10 cm or more (7.07%) and high histologic grade (10.08%).
claims.source_text: In a cohort of 7567 patients, 89 (1.18%) died of the disease. Significantly higher DFSP-specific mortality was associated with ≥10 cm tumor size and high histologic grade (7.07% and 10.08%, respectively) [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Proposed risk factors for recurrence and metastasis:** fibrosarcomatous change or high grade, older age, female sex, tumour of 10 cm or more, margins under 3 cm or positive, short time to recurrence, multiple recurrences, recent rapid growth and pain.
claims.source_text: Malignant transformation within DFSP (or high histologic grade), older age, being female, large primary tumor size (≥10 cm), narrow surgical margins of excision (<3 cm), surgical margin positivity for tumor cells, short time to recurrence, numerous recurrencies, a tumor that was recently rapidly enlarging, and presence of pain in the tumor have all been proposed as clinicopathologic risk factors for recurrence and metastasis.
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Surgery aiming at microscopically clear (R0) margins is first-line for resectable DFSP.** (A)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Micrographically controlled surgery is preferred** (B): Mohs or any technique that examines the whole peripheral and deep margin, usually on paraffin sections. Go down to deep fascia; 1–1.3 cm lateral margins then seem enough.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In comparative studies recurrence was 1.7% after Mohs versus 3.7% after wide excision (not significant),** and micrographic surgery spares more healthy tissue.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without micrographic surgery, excise with 2–3 cm lateral margins and the underlying fascia;** re-excise invaded margins until clear where feasible. (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Margin width matters in the review's data:** 1 cm left microscopic tumour in 70.7% of cases, 2 cm in 39.7%, 3 cm in 15.5% and 5 cm in 5.2%, and a meta-analysis of eight studies found margins of 3 cm or more lowered local relapse compared with narrower margins.
claims.source_text: An important piece of information came from a recent systematic review with a meta-analysis of eight eligible cohort and case-control studies: the performance of ≥3 cm margins in decreasing the local relapse rate was found to be highly significantly better (p < 0.00001) than that of <3 cm margins []. … a width of 1 cm around the primary tumor would have left microscopic residual mass in 70.7% of cases; a width of 2 cm in 39.7%; 3 cm, 15.5%; and 5 cm, 5.2% [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **S2 calls wide excision with at least 3 cm margins the gold standard for localised DFSP,** accepting functional or cosmetic cost, and says skin flaps should be considered when needed at any age. A systematic review gave only a weak recommendation for Mohs over wide excision; slow Mohs on paraffin sections appears to clear more completely.
claims.source_text: Wide radial surgical excision with at least 3 cm margins is the gold-standard curative treatment for localized DFSP but may result in functional impairment or cosmetic disfigurement. When needed, skin flap transplantations should be considered, regardless of the patient's age. … A systematic review gave a weak recommendation in favor of MMS over WLE for DFSP excision []. … There is accumulating evidence that modified MMS with horizontal en face sectioning of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded blocks, known as slow Mohs surgery, provides better results in terms of complete resection and tissue-sparing capabilities [,].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Reconstruct simply (direct closure, graft or healing by secondary intention), not with flaps,** so recurrence is seen early. (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resect recurrences with micrographically controlled surgery wherever possible.** (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Imatinib is decided by a multidisciplinary tumour board,** and given before surgery for primary or recurrent tumours that cannot be removed or only with unacceptable harm; operate if the tumour becomes resectable. (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start imatinib at 400 mg/day, increasing to 600–800 mg/day by response;** 400 and 800 mg gave the same response (67.5% vs 67.1%).
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imatinib's European approval covers inoperable primary, locally advanced or recurrent, and metastatic DFSP.** In fibrosarcomatous disease, confirm the fusion in the FS component (FISH or RT-PCR) before starting.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No chemotherapy regimen is established.** Advanced DFSP or FS-DFSP should go to an expert-centre tumour board, with trials where available.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imatinib response in advanced DFSP (systematic review, 152 patients):** complete 5.2%, partial 55.2%, stable 27.6%, progression 9.2%. The review judged 400 mg a day more appropriate than 800 mg because of adverse effects.
claims.source_text: A systematic review on imatinib for locally advanced or metastatic DFSP found that of 152 patients, complete response was observed in 8 (5.2%), partial response in 84 (55.2%), stable disease in 42 (27.6%), and progression in 14 (9.2%). A daily dose of 400 mg imatinib seems more appropriate than that of 800 mg; this is in relation to the adverse and severe adverse effects present in the vast majority of patients [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Imatinib can make advanced tumours operable:** in one series seven of fifteen (47%) had residual disease resected and stayed disease-free; in a French series of 27 locally advanced tumours given imatinib or pazopanib for a median 7 months, 24 (89%) went on to excision and 23 (85%) were disease-free at over 5 years' median follow-up.
claims.source_text: In some patients with advanced disease, imatinib was effective in decreasing the tumor size and making the lesion operable. Seven (47%) out of these fifteen patients underwent resection of residual disease and remained free of disease []. … In a French study from 2021, 27 patients with locally advanced DFSP received the tyrosine kinase inhibitors imatinib or pazopanib for a median duration of 7 months; 24 (89%) of them then underwent surgical excision, and during an over 5-year median follow-up, 23 (85%) patients were disease-free [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Radiotherapy never replaces adequate surgery and is not given after clear (R0) excision of non-transformed DFSP** (B). It may be added for close margins, recurrence or aggressive subtypes, and as salvage for positive margins.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Curative doses are usually 60 Gy for microscopic and 70 Gy for macroscopic residual disease,** in conventional 2 Gy daily fractions.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Radiotherapy detail (S2):** treat the tumour and any scars with 3–5 cm safety margins, 2 Gy five times a week to 60–66 Gy for microscopic or 66–70 Gy for macroscopic residual tumour; 50 Gy may suffice for palliation. It may be a primary option when wide excision would cause major cosmetic or functional harm.
claims.source_text: Such a therapy may also be considered a primary treatment option for patients in whom wide excision would result in significant cosmetic or functional impairment. The target volume includes the tumor itself plus any scar(s) from previous surgery plus safety margins of 3-5 cm. With curative intent, a single dose of 2 Gy is usually administered five times a week for a total dose of 60-66 Gy (when microscopic evidence of tumor cells exists) or 66-70 Gy (when there is macroscopic evidence of residual tumor). In a palliative setting, and depending on tumor site and surrounding vital structures, a total dose of 50 Gy may be sufficient [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Adjuvant radiotherapy to the tumour bed after excision is not recommended:** a systematic review of 12 retrospective studies showed only a weak trend to fewer local recurrences.
claims.source_text: Adjuvant radiation of the tumor bed following the excision of DFSP is not recommended. A systematic review of 12 retrospective clinical trials showed only a weak trend towards lower local recurrence rates after adjuvant postoperative radiotherapy compared to surgery alone [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **FS-DFSP goes to a sarcoma tumour board; standard treatment is complete excision with margins of at least 2 cm.** Micrographic surgery can be considered but is unproven here.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **S2 states Mohs surgery is not indicated when there is fibrosarcomatous transformation.**
claims.source_text: Yet the use of MMS is not indicated for patients with fibrosarcomatous transformation [,].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Recurrences come late (median 55 months).** After complete excision with low-risk pathology, examine the site every 6 months for 3 years, then every 12 months to year 5 (C). With high-risk features, add MRI 6-monthly for 2 years, then 6–12-monthly to year 5 and at least yearly to year 10. Teach self-examination.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Routine chest X-ray in follow-up was not useful for typical DFSP** (Dutch study), only for fibrosarcomatous tumours with their higher lung-metastasis risk. Re-biopsy anything suspicious.
claims.source_text: In a Dutch study, routine chest X-ray during follow-up did not seem to be useful in patients with typical DFSP, except for those who had fibrosarcomatous changes and thus a relatively high risk for lung metastases []. Any suspicious region requires rebiopsy [].
claims.locator: Jozwik M, Bednarczuk K, Osierda Z, et al. (narrative review), Cancers (Basel) 2024;16(18):3124 (doi 10.3390/cancers16183124), 'Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans: An Updated Review of the Literature', published 11 September 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11430793/, retrieved 2026-09-24
